item.title: Change in Publication Model
item.description: Dear all greetings from the editorial team of Journal of Neonatal Surgery As you have seen, we have moved to the latest code of Open Journal System. However, all the users could not be shifted to the new version. We are in process of shifting all the under processing manuscripts to the new system. Users are however requested to check if their account is not shifted, they can register a new account as an author and reviewer or reader. The journal has decided to pursue Issue free publishing model

item.title: Login issues with the JNS website
item.description: Dear All, Greetings. We have learned from many colleagues that they are facing login problems for the JNS website. We are on it for solving the issue. Clearing your browser cache or using another browser usually solve this problem. Regards Team JNS

item.title: Training opportunity as Assistant Editor at JNS
item.description: The editorial team of the Journal of Neonatal Surgery invites applications from interested Pediatric/Neonatal surgeons/trainees for the training opportunity as Assistant Editor of the JNS. Junior consultants or senior residents of pediatric/neonatal surgery with at least 5 publications will be preferred. There are 4-6 slots for this position. item.title: Journal of Neonatal Surgery now on Scopus
item.description: We are pleased to announce that the Journal of Neonatal Surgery is now indexed on Scopus for its content coverage. We are thankful to our authors, reviewers, readers, and editorial team members for their efforts.

item.title: Over 2000 citations of JNS
item.description: The editorial team is pleased to announce achieving a milestone of over 2000 citations by the Journal of Neonatal Surgery since its inception. Kindly see the google scholar citation report by clicking the link given as under: https://scholar.google.com.pk/citations?user=rsxu5owAAAAJ&hl=en

item.title: Most Cited Publication
item.description: The editorial team of the Journal of Neonatal Surgery congratulates Dr. Lalitha Krishnan for being the author of "Pain relief in neonates"- the most cited publication of the Journal of Neonatal Surgery. It has been cited 50 times as per Google Scholar since its publication.

item.title: Collaboration with PSON
item.description: The Editorial team of the Journal of Neonatal Surgery feels immense pleasure to announce its collaboration with the Paediatric Surgery Online Society (PSON). We are grateful to Dr. Antonio Cutrupi for this endorsement.
